title: structured output: add constrained-decoding backends (CFG, regex, token-aware decoders)
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: We need a pluggable constrained-decoding stack to support structured-output constraints (CFG/grammar, regex, and token-aware constraints) for the Redwood API and the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR introduces a constrained-decoding backend abstraction and three reference backends: a grammar/CFG backend, a fast regex-based backend, and a token-aware regex backend that handles tokenizer boundary edge-cases during streaming.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a ConstrainedDecoder interface in serving/runtime that allows multiple backend implementations to be swapped at runtime.
- Implements a CFG backend (supports annotated productions, canonicalization, and partial-match streaming hooks).
- Implements a regex backend optimized for common patterns (dates, IDs, JSON fragments) using compiled DFA and early-abort heuristics.
- Implements a token-aware regex backend that rewrites regexes to be aware of token boundaries and handles partial tokens emitted during streaming. This fixes tokenization edge-cases where a regex would match across token splits or miss matches because of subtoken splits.
- Adds integration with the OpenAI compatibility layer so constrained outputs via the `structured_output` param are honored by both the native Redwood API and the OpenAI shim.
- Adds extensive unit and integration tests that exercise streaming, partial-token scenarios, and mixed-constraint cases (CFG + regex).
- Adds examples and docs for how to select backends and recommendations for throughput vs. strictness tradeoffs.

Key implementation notes:
- The ConstrainedDecoder is a thin ABI with methods: start(stream_ctx), accept_token(token_id, token_text), finish(), suggest_fallbacks(). Backends maintain streaming state and can indicate early-failure or early-success to the sampler.
- CFG backend: uses a compact, precompiled production table. It supports prefix-matching for streaming and incremental parse checkpointing to avoid re-parsing on re-rollouts. It is conservative in accepting output until the parse is unambiguous to avoid partiality in structured responses.
- Regex backend: compiles patterns into DFA where possible and uses a rolling window to match fragments. It is the fastest for many common constraints but can be brittle with subtokens unless used with token-aware mode.
- Token-aware regex backend: rewrites patterns to account for tokenization boundaries (handles BPE and byte-level subtokens), using tokenization metadata to ensure matches only when token boundaries align and to reconstruct candidate match spans that straddle partial tokens during streaming.
- Backends expose a `confidence` metric used by the sampler to prefer less-restrictive fallbacks when strict constraints cannot be satisfied under latency SLOs.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for each backend including fuzz tests for tokenizer edge-cases.
- Integration tests that run constrained decoding against the OpenAI-compat endpoint in both immediate and streaming modes.
- Performance microbenchmarks comparing unconstrained sampling vs. DFA-regex and CFG across typical payloads.
- CI showed an intermittent flake in streaming-integration-tests on linux-x86; re-ran the suite and it passed.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- serving/runtime/constrained_decoder.h/cpp  (new interface and adapter)
- serving/runtime/backends/cfg_backend.cc/.h
- serving/runtime/backends/regex_backend.cc/.h
- serving/runtime/backends/token_aware_regex_backend.cc/.h
- api/openai_shim/constraints_adapter.py (integration glue)
- docs/structured-output/backends.md (usage + perf guidance)
- tests/unit/test_constrained_backends.py
- tests/integration/test_streaming_constraints.py

Backward compatibility and migration: This is additive. Default behaviour remains unchanged unless a request includes `structured_output` or a config enables constrained-decoding. The OpenAI shim honors the same parameter by default for parity with earlier experiments.

Known limitations / Future work:
- CFG backend does not yet support left-recursive grammars; a follow-up will add support or pre-flattening tooling.
- Token-aware regex engine increases memory per-request when tracking token metadata; we'll iterate on the memory footprint in a subsequent PR.
- More work to surface fine-grained failure reasons in API errors for better developer DX.

Overall this PR provides a pluggable, test-covered implementation to enable production-grade structured output constraints with attention to streaming and tokenizer edge cases.
commits: initial: add constrained_decoder interface and adapter (serving/runtime)
implement cfg backend with streaming prefix-matching
implement regex backend with DFA compilation and rolling window
implement token-aware regex backend and token metadata plumbing
integration: wire OpenAI shim to constrained-decoder API
tests: add unit and integration tests + microbench harness
docs: usage guide and backend selection recommendations
fix: memory leak in token metadata buffer (addressed during review)
review_comments: Ethan Li: Overall looks good. Please add more tests around subtokens split mid-regex match (BPE and byte-level).
Priya Shah: Added fuzz tests and an explicit test case for a known BPE split scenario (test_fuzz_bpe_split).
Marco Ruiz: The CFG streaming prefix logic looks sound, but can we reduce allocations when checkpointing? Consider arena allocation or reusing parse buffers.
Priya Shah: Reworked checkpointing to use arena allocator for per-request parse state; benchmarks show ~12% lower p99 memory in the microbench.
Ava Thompson: Please document the tradeoffs and how to select regex vs token-aware regex in docs/backends.md.
Priya Shah: Expanded docs section with recommended defaults and examples for date/ID/JSON constraints.
Ethan Li: CI showed an intermittent failure in integration streaming on linux-x86; re-run fixes it but leave a note in the test harness to retry flaky tests once before failing.
Priya Shah: Added a retry wrapper for the most flaky integration test and a TODO to investigate root cause (ENG-1907).
Marco Ruiz: LGTM, approving after minor nits fixed.
release_notes: Add pluggable constrained-decoding backends (CFG, regex, token-aware regex) for structured outputs. Enables token-aware regex matching to avoid tokenizer boundary edge-cases in streaming. Backwards compatible and opt-in via structured_output config.
